sentences.text: 3.3 Parameters and hyperparameters
sentences.say: 3.3 Parameters and hyperparameters

sentences.text: Parameters are the numbers the algorithm learns: w and b in a line, the weights in a neural network.
sentences.say: Parameters are the numbers the algorithm learns: w and b in a line, the weights in a neural network.

sentences.text: Hyperparameters are settings you choose before training and that training does not change: the learning rate, the number of passes over the data (epochs), K in nearest neighbours, the regularization strength, the polynomial degree.
sentences.say: Hyperparameters are settings you choose before training and that training does not change: the learning rate, the number of passes over the data (epochs), K in nearest neighbours, the regularization strength, the polynomial degree.

sentences.text: You find good hyperparameters by trying values and measuring on held-out data, not by guessing (Shaw Talebi).
sentences.say: You find good hyperparameters by trying values and measuring on held-out data, not by guessing (Shaw Talebi).

sentences.text: 3.4 Train, validation and test sets
sentences.say: 3.4 Train, validation and test sets

sentences.text: A model that scores well on the examples it was fitted to has proved nothing, just as a student who sees the exam questions in advance proves nothing.
sentences.say: A model that scores well on the examples it was fitted to has proved nothing, just as a student who sees the exam questions in advance proves nothing.

sentences.text: You need data the model has never seen:
sentences.say: You need data the model has never seen:

sentences.text: Two rules that save careers.
sentences.say: Two rules that save careers.

sentences.text: First, fit any preparation step (such as scaling) on the training set only, then apply it to the others.
sentences.say: First, fit any preparation step (such as scaling) on the training set only, then apply it to the others.

sentences.text: Fitting it on everything lets information from the test rows leak into training.
sentences.say: Fitting it on everything lets information from the test rows leak into training.

sentences.text: Second, for data that has a time order, such as loans, split by date: train on the past, test on the future.
sentences.say: Second, for data that has a time order, such as loans, split by date: train on the past, test on the future.

sentences.text: A random split lets the model peek at the future and flatters it.
sentences.say: A random split lets the model peek at the future and flatters it.

sentences.text: 3.5 Data quality
sentences.say: 3.5 Data quality

sentences.text: Machine learning is only as good as its data: garbage in, garbage out.
sentences.say: Machine learning is only as good as its data: garbage in, garbage out.

sentences.text: Good data has quantity (too few examples lead to overfitting, Chapter 11) and quality (Shaw Talebi):

sentences.say: Accurate.

sentences.text: An age of 35 that should be 53, or an income of $12,000 that is really per month, teaches the model something false.

sentences.text: Three traps that are especially common in lending:
sentences.say: Three traps that are especially common in lending:

sentences.text: Selection bias.
sentences.say: Selection bias.

sentences.text: You only know whether people repaid if you approved them.
sentences.say: You only know whether people repaid if you approved them.

sentences.text: A model trained on approved loans has never seen the rejected ones.
sentences.say: A model trained on approved loans has never seen the rejected ones.

sentences.text: Leakage.
sentences.say: Leakage.

sentences.text: A feature that is only known after the outcome, such as a collections status, makes a model look brilliant in testing and useless in production.
sentences.say: A feature that is only known after the outcome, such as a collections status, makes a model look brilliant in testing and useless in production.

sentences.text: Always ask: would I have this value at the moment of the decision?
sentences.say: Always ask: would I have this value at the moment of the decision?

sentences.text: Label noise.
sentences.say: Label noise.

sentences.text: The target itself can be wrong or defined inconsistently, for example "default" meaning 60 days late in one system and 90 in another.
sentences.say: The target itself can be wrong or defined inconsistently, for example "default" meaning 60 days late in one system and 90 in another.

sentences.text: 3.6 Always measure a baseline
sentences.say: 3.6 Always measure a baseline

sentences.text: A baseline is the simplest sensible prediction: for regression, predict the average of the training targets; for classification, predict the most common class.
sentences.say: A baseline is the simplest sensible prediction: for regression, predict the average of the training targets; for classification, predict the most common class.

sentences.text: If 95% of offers are accepted, a model that always says "accepted" is 95% accurate and completely useless.
sentences.say: If 95 percent of offers are accepted, a model that always says "accepted" is 95 percent accurate and completely useless.

sentences.text: Your model has to beat the baseline by a margin that matters, or it is not earning its complexity.
sentences.say: Your model has to beat the baseline by a margin that matters, or it is not earning its complexity.
